items.front: How is the President elected?
items.back: Indirectly, by an electoral college of elected MPs + elected MLAs (incl. Delhi & Puducherry), by proportional representation via single transferable vote (Art 54-55).
items.examPoint: President — indirect election, electoral college & STV (Art 54-55)
items.source: Arts 54-55

items.front: Which Article gives the President ordinance-making power, and when?
items.back: Article 123 — only when Parliament (either House) is not in session; ordinance must be laid before Parliament and lapses 6 weeks after it reassembles.
items.source: Art 123

items.front: Cap on the size of the Council of Ministers?
items.back: Total ministers incl. PM must not exceed 15% of Lok Sabha strength (91st Amendment, 2003). Ranks are NOT specified in the Constitution.
items.examPoint: Council of Ministers — Art 74/75, 91st CAA 15% cap, collective responsibility
items.source: UPSC 2022 PYQ; 91st Amendment 2003

items.front: Which powers are exclusive to the Lok Sabha?
items.back: No-confidence motion and originating Money Bills. (Impeaching the President and ratifying Emergency are NOT LS-exclusive.)
items.source: UPSC 2022 PYQ

items.front: Max strength of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?
items.back: Lok Sabha max 552 (530 states + 20 UTs + 2 Anglo-Indian seats, ended by 104th Amendment 2019; effectively 550 now); Rajya Sabha max 250.
items.examPoint: Lok Sabha — strength, term & composition (Art 81/83, 104th Amdt)
items.source: Arts 80, 81; 104th Amendment 2019

items.front: Who certifies a Money Bill, and what is the Rajya Sabha's role?
items.back: The Lok Sabha Speaker certifies (final). Money Bills (Art 110) originate only in LS; RS can only recommend, must return within 14 days.
items.examPoint: Money Bill (Art 110) vs Ordinary & Financial bills
items.source: UPSC 2018 PYQ; Art 110

items.front: Rajya Sabha has EQUAL power with Lok Sabha in what?
items.back: Amending the Constitution (Art 368). Money Bills and Amendment Bills are excluded from a joint sitting.
items.examPoint: Rajya Sabha — composition, permanent house, 1/3 retire (Art 80)
items.source: UPSC 2020 PYQ; Art 368

items.front: Joint sitting (Art 108) — who presides and what majority?
items.back: The Lok Sabha Speaker presides; the bill is passed by a simple majority of members present and voting.
items.examPoint: Joint sitting of Parliament (Art 108) — exclusions & instances
items.source: UPSC 2015 PYQ; Art 108

items.front: Largest parliamentary committee and its composition?
items.back: Estimates Committee — 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. (PAC = 22: 15 LS + 7 RS.)
items.source: UPSC 2014 PYQ

items.front: Can the Attorney General participate in Parliament?
items.back: Yes — the AG (Art 76/88) has the right to speak in either House and its committees, but cannot vote.
items.examPoint: Council of Ministers — Art 74/75, 91st CAA 15% cap, collective responsibility
items.source: UPSC 2013 PYQ; Arts 76, 88

items.front: Effect of Lok Sabha dissolution on a Bill pending only in the Rajya Sabha?
items.back: It does NOT lapse (never passed by LS). A Bill passed by both Houses awaiting assent also does not lapse.
items.examPoint: Effect of dissolution of Lok Sabha on pending bills
items.source: UPSC 2016 PYQ; Art 107

items.front: Anti-defection law — where, and who decides disqualification?
items.back: Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985); decided by the presiding officer, with no fixed time-frame prescribed.
items.examPoint: Presiding officers — Speaker's powers, casting vote & anti-defection
items.source: UPSC 2022 PYQ; 10th Schedule

items.front: Max gap between two parliamentary sessions?
items.back: Six months (Art 85). Three sessions by convention (Budget, Monsoon, Winter) — not constitutionally mandated.
items.source: UPSC 2020 PYQ; Art 85

items.front: Zero Hour vs Question Hour?
items.back: Question Hour = first hour (starred oral / unstarred written). Zero Hour = Indian innovation (since 1962), not in the rules.
items.examPoint: Parliamentary devices — Question Hour, Zero Hour & motions
items.source: Parliamentary practice

items.front: Vice-President — role and how removed?
items.back: Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Art 64); removal resolution can be initiated only in the Rajya Sabha (effective majority), then agreed by Lok Sabha.
items.source: Arts 63-67

items.front: Key financial features of the MPLAD Scheme?
items.back: Non-lapsable & carried forward; for durable community assets; a share earmarked for SC & ST areas; at least 10% of works inspected at the district level.
items.examPoint: MPLADS — non-lapsable funds, durable assets & inspection norms
items.source: review-v2 R2

items.front: Which committee & year relate to the Department of Personnel?
items.back: The N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar Committee urged personnel reform; the Department of Personnel was set up in 1970 under the Prime Minister (ARC-I: 1966).
items.examPoint: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar Committee & Department of Personnel (1970)
items.source: review-v2 R2

items.front: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha — election & removal?
items.back: Elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members (Art 93); removable by an effective-majority resolution after 14 days' notice (Art 94); presides when the Speaker's post is vacant.
items.source: review-v2 R2

items.front: Has any President of India been impeached?
items.back: No. The Article 61 impeachment procedure has never been used against any President.

items.back: The President of India (exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers).

items.front: True or false: The office of Whip is set up by the 1998 Leaders and Chief Whips Act.
items.back: False. The Whip rests on convention only. The 1998 Act just gives facilities.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The government Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha is a Minister of State.
items.back: False. It is the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, of Cabinet rank.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A Private Member's Bill becomes government policy once the House passes it.
items.back: False. It shows only the mover's view, even after it passes.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Public and private bills pass through the same stages in the House.
items.back: True. Both follow the same general procedure and stages.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on dissolution.
items.back: True. It lapses when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, not passed by the Lok Sabha, lapses on dissolution.
items.back: False. It does NOT lapse; the Rajya Sabha is never dissolved.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A bill returned by the President lapses if the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
items.back: False. A returned bill does not lapse, even after dissolution.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Appropriation Act carries an automatic repeal clause.
items.back: False. It has no automatic repeal clause.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund can be discussed but not voted.
items.back: True. Examples: President's pay, judges' salaries, CAG, debt charges.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The President has a suspensive veto over Money Bills.
items.back: False. On a Money Bill he can only assent or withhold. No return.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: India's pocket veto has a time limit of 10 days, as in the USA.
items.back: False. India has no time limit. The US pocket veto is 10 days.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: MPs' freedom from arrest covers criminal cases and preventive detention.
items.back: False. It covers civil cases only, during the session and 40 days around it.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A House can punish outsiders, not only members, for contempt.
items.back: True. It can reprimand, admonish or imprison members and outsiders.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: "Breach of privilege" is wider than "contempt of the House".
items.back: False. Contempt is wider. Every breach is a contempt, not the reverse.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Removal of the Vice-President must start in the Rajya Sabha.
items.back: True. A Rajya Sabha resolution starts it; the Lok Sabha then agrees.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Rajya Sabha has equal power in approving all three emergencies.
items.back: True. Also equal in amendments, CAG reports and judges' removal.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Estimates Committee is a tool of financial control.
items.back: True. 30 Lok Sabha members; it suggests economies in estimates.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The PAC chairman comes from the Opposition by a rule of procedure.
items.back: False. It is by convention, since 1967.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Art 255: an Act is void if the President's previous sanction was not taken.
items.back: False. Later assent cures it. The Act stays valid.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Only the President can pardon a death sentence.
items.back: True. A Governor can suspend, remit or commute it, but not pardon it.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Prorogation makes pending bills lapse.
items.back: False. Bills do not lapse on prorogation. Only dissolution can lapse them.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Delimitation orders can be challenged in court.
items.back: False. They have the force of law and courts cannot question them.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Delimitation Commission also fixes SC and ST reserved seats.
items.back: True. It draws boundaries and identifies reserved seats.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The President's electoral college includes nominated MPs.
items.back: False. Only elected MPs, elected MLAs, and Delhi and Puducherry MLAs.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Art 80(3) lets the President nominate Rajya Sabha members for sport.
items.back: False. The fields are literature, science, art and social service.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: Who presides over the parliamentary forums?
items.back: The Speaker, except the Forum on Population and Public Health, presided over by the Rajya Sabha Chairman. First forum: water, 2005.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan
